ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement, annual, and event-driven screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Colombian domestic restrictive lists. PEP status is verified under Colombian PEP regulations and documentary evidence of source of funds and source of wealth is retained for at least five years after the commercial relation ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) via the local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names in Colombia must be expressed in Latin script; the name normally appears in Spanish or in a foreign language transliterated into Latin characters. The name must not be deceptive regarding the corporate type and must include the designation 'S.A.S.' or 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada'. Accented Spanish characters are accepted; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name reservation must be challenged by requesting the written ground of objection from the Chamber of Commerce, then filing a recurso de reposición with the same registry officer within ten business days and, in the alternative/subsidiario, recurso de apelación before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio. As a fallback, the applicant may file a constitutional derecho de petición under Ley 1755 de 2015. If the reservation expires after 30 days without use, a new clearance must be requested; extension is only available if the applicable chamber tariff expressly permits renewal before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally acceptable for the nominal S.A.S. registered office and for receiving legal notifications, but it cannot satisfy INVIMA's physical-plant requirement for sterile medical device manufacturing; the production facility and quality-control laboratories must be physically located in Colombia and pass inspection before the sanitary registration is issued.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (about 10%) for the virtual administrative office absent complaint; high (above 70%) for the manufacturing facility during INVIMA sanitary registration of the sterile nitrile examination gloves, with a 20–35% annual post-license re-inspection probability.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Colombian Commercial Code (Código de Comercio, Decreto 410/1971) as amended; Law 1258 of 2008 regulating Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.); Article 353 et seq. of the Commercial Code; Law 1429 of 2010 (formalization incentives)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) of the jurisdiction of the registered office, under the supervision of the Superintendencia de Sociedades (conflict only in matters of judicial intervention)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation document) filed for registration in the Mercantile Registry; alternatively a public deed executed before a notary
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required for S.A.S.; capital may be subscribed and paid in full or in successive instalments within two years from the date of incorporation (Law 1258/2008, Art. 9). Monetary contributions must be deposited in a Colombian financial institution if the bylaws so provide, but no statutory escrow is mandatory. Shares may be issued for cash, tangible or intangible assets, or future services subject to specific rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 001 OF THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S.: The undersigned sole shareholder, exercising powers under Law 1258 of 2008, resolves: First, to subscribe the unissued share capital comprising 1,000 common shares of nominal value COP 1,000 each, fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the bylaws; no monetary payment is required beyond the assets contributed as disclosed. Second, to adopt as the legal registered office the premises located at Carrera 100 No. 15-55, Bogotá D.C., and to entrust its administration to the legal representative. Third, to appoint [Name LastName] as President, Legal Representative, and [Name LastName] as Compliance Officer, granting them broad powers under commercial law. Fourth, to authorize the filing of registration before the Chamber of Commerce and all subsequent governmental licenses. This resolution takes immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business name homologation and availability certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio principal (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) through the online RUES portal or window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request through the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) online platform or in person at the Chamber of Commerce. Specify the desired corporate name, the legal form (S.A.S.), and principal activity. Pay the nominal search fee and obtain the Certificado de Homonimia certifying that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity. The certificate must be obtained within 30 days before filing of the incorporation document.
required_dossiers: Application form for name search
Valid identification document of the applicant or requesting shareholder
Power of attorney (notarized) if filed through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, the applicant may appeal the decision by presenting arguments or modifying the corporate name; new search may be filed immediately. A formal reconsideration request can be lodged within 5 days with the Chamber of Commerce's legal department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the private incorporation document (or public deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (if public deed option elected) or directly before the Chamber of Commerce for private document; lawyer or authorized legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the private incorporation document (Documento Privado de Constitución) containing the full bylaws, corporate purpose (including manufacture of synthetic nitrile gloves), registered office, internal rules, share capital subscription, identification of shareholders, and appointment of officers. Execute voluntarily and freely, with signatures of all shareholders or their authorized representatives. If a public deed is preferred, has the document executed before a Colombian notary and obtain a certified public deed.
required_dossiers: Valid evidence of name availability certificate
Identity documents of all shareholders (cédula for Colombians; passport for non-residents)
Certificate of domicile or lease/ownership title of the registered office premises
Power of attorney (if signed by attorney-in-fact)
RUT of each shareholder if previously registered with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber of Commerce or notary objects to form or substance, correct the document in accordance with the Attorney's observations and re-submit; there is no separate appeal for notarization defects, but the document can be replaced within 10 days. For substantive omissions, add a clarification or an act of amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed private incorporation document or public deed along with the pre-scanned application forms for mercantile registration (Formulario de Registro). Pay the registration tariff (derechos de registro) set by the Chamber of Commerce, based on capital amount and current tariff table. After review, the Chamber assigns a Mercantile Registration Number and issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal.
required_dossiers: Original or copy of the private incorporation document or notarial deed
Certificado de Homonimia (name search certificate)
Formulario de Registro Único Empresarial (FUES)
Payment receipt for registration fees
Applicable stamp tax (timbre) payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry refuses registration, the applicant can cure the deficiency and re-submit within the legal term (10 days normally), or file a review request before the Superintendencia de Sociedades within 5 days after notification. Registration automatically cures defects unless fraud is established.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax identification (NIT) and single tax registry (RUT) enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) via regional office or online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly formed company with DIAN to obtain the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT). Complete Formulario 001 (Registro Único Tributario) electronically using the pre-registered information of the legal representative. Select the tax obligations: income tax (before 2023, later adopted under Law 2277), sales tax (IVA), and industry and commerce tax procedures (ICA) to be reported to the municipality. The NIT is issued immediately after validation; the RUT must be updated whenever changes occur.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation issued by the Chamber of Commerce
Identification document of the legal representative
Proof of the physical establishment address (utility bill or lease contract)
Formulario 001 duly completed and signed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NIT/RUT application is rejected or suspended, the applicant may correct the information and re-submit electronically; an appeal in reconsideration may be filed with DIAN within 10 days if the rejection persists. Incorrect classifications can be adjusted by filing an amendment to the RUT.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal operating license and land-use compatibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Municipal or Local Mayor's Office, Secretaría de Planeación and/or Secretaría de Gobierno (depending on municipality)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a certificate of intended land use (uso de suelo) from the city planning department confirming that the selected registered office and manufacturing plant are compatible with the industrial zoning and manufacturing of medical gloves. Then submit an application for a business operating license (Licencia de Funcionamiento or Registro Sanitario from the point of view of industrial operation if required locally). For industrial establishments, the application typically includes plant layout and environmental compatibility statement.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation
RUT notification
Copy of lease agreement or property title of the industrial premises
Architectural/engineering layout of the production area
Certificate of land use (zeroing or equivalently 'Uso de Suelo')
Payment of municipal fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the land-use certificate is unfavorable, the applicant may appeal the classification within the municipality or seek a special industrial zoning authorization through the local planning authority. Refusal of the operating license may be contested via an administrative appeal within 10 days, requiring additional environmental or structural documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Health authorization and sanitary registration of sterile medical gloves
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INVIMA (Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for Registro Sanitario de Dispositivo Médico (Consecution of sanitary registration) for sterile latex and nitrile examination gloves under Decreto 4725/2005 (as amended) and relevant Ministry of Health regulations. Include the technical file detailing sterilization method (e.g., ethylene oxide), biocompatibility testing, shelf-life, and conformity with recognized standards (ISO 11193, ISO 13485, EN 455). Provide proof of establishment approval as a manufacturer and compliance with Good Manufacturing Practices (BPM/GMP). Pay the INVIMA tariff and await assessment, which may involve factory inspection.
required_dossiers: Technical dossier (device description, materials, design)
Evidence of quality management system (ISO 13485 certification)
GMP manufacturing authorization from the health authority
Sterilization validation report
Biological and chemical safety test reports
Labeling and instructions for use
Payment receipt of INVIMA fees
Certificates of free sale or prior registration in another country (if available)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If INVIMA issues a technical requirement or rejects the registration, the applicant may, within 30 days, supplement the file with additional studies or tests, or file an appeal for reconsideration with INVIMA (objeción or recurso de reposición). If administrative silence occurs, petition action may be used under the Code of Administrative Procedure. For unauthorized or expired licenses, immediate corrective filing is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social / INVIMA (for medical device manufacturing) and Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (for corporate compliance, not industrial licensing)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Sanitario para Dispositivo Médico (Medical Device Sanitary Registration) and Manufacturing Establishment Authorization

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: ANLA - Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (national level) or Regional Autonomous Corporation (CAR) for municipal/regional environmental permitting
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Registration and environmental compliance statement (Diagnóstico Ambiental de Alternativas is not required for moderate PPE manufacturing); may be exempt from full EIA if the plant is small-scale and implements best available techniques, but requires environmental control measures for wastewater, air emissions and solid hazardous waste under Law 99/1993 and Decree 1076/2015.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds: wastewater pH 6-9, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) ≤ 200 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand (COD) ≤ 400 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 80 mg/L before discharge to sewer (Resolution 0631/2015); VOC emissions from drying/curing ovens must meet a limit of 50 mg C/Nm3 and capture efficiency ≥85% (Resolution 909/2008); particulate matter from glove powdering (if any) below 50 mg/m3; all hazardous residues (e.g., coagulant sludges, chlorine) must be handled under Resolution 1023/2005 and registry with the environmental authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos (local Fire Department) verifying emergency exits, fire extinguishing systems, and flammable-liquid containment; structural load inspection and seismic compliance certificate for industrial plant issued by the local building control department; occupational safety and health clearance (SGSST) under Resolution 0312/2019, including certification of industrial hygienist program and work permit regime for hazardous activities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - national tax and customs authority; operational portal MUISCA accessible at www.dian.gov.co and muisca.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the S.A.S. before the local Cámara de Comercio through the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE); the foreign parent executes the formation deed (private document suffices unless real property is contributed). Step 2: File the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) via VUE-MUISCA using the legal representative's digital certificate; DIAN assigns the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria). Step 3: In the RUT, declare the economic activity CIU 3250, mark the taxpayer as IVA-responsable and as 'exportador' for customs purposes, and confirm the foreign-exchange obligation. Step 4: Obtain the DIAN digital signature certificate and register an authorized electronic-invoicing software provider (or use DIAN's free electronic invoicing platform). Step 5: Before first shipment, complete INVIMA sanitary registration and GMP certification for the sterile nitrile glove line and enrol in the VUCE (Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior); subsequent export declarations (DEX) are filed electronically with DIAN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope / Tax_Exempt_Zone_option / Pass_Through_Eligible: Not applicable. The S.A.S. is a full Colombian tax resident (incorporation test) taxed on worldwide income at the 35% headline rate (Arts. 12 and 240 E.T.), with a foreign tax credit. Dividends remitted to the foreign shareholder trigger Colombian source withholding at distribution. Tax_Exempt_Zone: Zona Franca user status is available and reduces manufacturing income to a 20% CIT rate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Colombian law. Available elections: (i) Zona Franca (free-zone) user election under Art. 240-1 E.T. - a DIAN/Comité Nacional de Zonas Francas resolution granting a 20% CIT rate plus customs duty and VAT suspension on inputs, subject to an investment/employment undertaking; (ii) Régimen Simple de Tributación (Arts. 908-917 E.T.) for eligible businesses with prior-year gross income not exceeding 100,000 UVT (approx. COP 4,706.5 million in 2024); exporters generally decline this election to preserve VAT credit and refund rights; (iii) advance pricing agreement (APA) with DIAN to fix transfer-pricing margins for related-party cross-border purchases of raw materials and licensed technology.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia) – Departamento de Cambios Internacionales; foreign exchange framework established by Law 9 of 1991 (Estatuto Cambiario), Decree 1735 of 1993, Resolución Externa 1 of 2018 of Banco de la República, and Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83; operational oversight shared with Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) and DIAN for transaction filings and sanctions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a free-floating exchange rate regime with the TRM (Tasa Representativa del Mercado) published daily by Banco de la República. Current-account operations (goods, services, royalties) are fully convertible but must be channeled through the 'mercado cambiario' via authorized intermediaries (commercial banks, financial corporations, and stock brokerage firms). Capital-account convertibility is substantially unrestricted for foreign direct investment (FDI), portfolio investment, and external credit, provided the operation is channeled through an authorized intermediary and registered with Banco de la República (Registro de Inversiones Internacionales). Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is lawful at 100% of formally declared dividends provided the FDI is duly registered, applicable dividend withholding tax (generally 5%, with a 7.5% rate in defined cases) is paid to DIAN, and the remittance is declared through the exchange declaration mechanism; no minimum holding period applies to FDI since Decree 2086 of 2003. Non-channeled operations lose legal validity for foreign-exchange purposes and are subject to exchange fines by DIAN.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Resolución Externa 1 de 2018 (Articles 75-79), exporters of goods must channel ('canalizar') all export proceeds through the Colombian foreign-exchange market within six (6) months following the shipment date (fecha de embarque) or within four (4) months following the contractual collection due date, whichever is later. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0% – there is no statutory obligation to convert FX into Colombian pesos; the exporter may sell the currency to the market at TRM or credit it to an authorized foreign-currency account maintained with a local authorized intermediary. The obligation is a 100% canalization duty: the export must be named in the Declaración de Cambio Formulario No. 4, matched to the DIAN export declaration and bill of lading; failure to channel within the statutory window triggers exchange-control fines and may jeopardize the exporter's access to FX rights.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account (COP) and FDI Capital Escrow / Share-Subscription Temporary Deposit Account, plus Foreign-Currency Deposit Account
Operational Current Account (COP) and Capital Escrow / Share-Capital Deposit Account
Operational Current Account (COP), Capital Escrow / Temporary FDI Deposit Account, and Trade Finance Facility (LC Origination)
Operational Current Account (COP) and FX Hedging/Trade Account
Operational Current Account (COP), Cross-Border Cash Management Account, and Capital Escrow Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as the primary treasury rail. Colombia does not recognize the EU/UK 'EMI' category; non-bank electronic payment firms (Nequi, RappiPay, Lulo Bank) are licensed as SEDPES (Sociedades Especializadas en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos) and cannot hold export FX, open FDI capital escrow accounts, or supply commercial letters of credit. Foreign EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Revolut Business) may serve as collection-only rails for marketplace receivables, but any export proceeds held offshore must still be repatriated to an authorized Colombian intermediary and channeled through the 'mercado cambiario' within the statutory deadline; unrepatriated offshore FMIs are not a valid canalization. The compliant architecture is a local tier-1 bank account paired with an EMI for convenience collections and immediate onward transfer to the local bank; the EMI cannot legally substitute for an authorized intermediary.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a foreign-owned SAS with non-resident shareholders, in-person KYC interviews are the general rule. The legal representative must attend the bank branch physically for biometric verification, signature-card execution, and the first exchange declaration; a local attorney-in-fact may substitute if the foreign apostilled power of attorney expressly grants banking, treasury, FX, and account-signatory powers and is registered with the Cámara de Comercio. Fully remote corporate onboarding is only accepted on a case-by-case basis at tier-1 banks for video-KYC of the foreign parent's director where the UBO holds an e-passport or Colombian cédula; it is materially rare for a 100% foreign-UBO structure. Anticipate two to four weeks from document submission to account activation, including apostille, Chamber of Commerce registration of the representative, UBO declaration, and internal SAGRILAFT approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) or direct shareholder resident in a FATF grey-listed or Colombian enhanced-monitoring jurisdiction (e.g., Panama, UAE, Malta), triggering enhanced due diligence (EDD) under SFC Circular Básica Jurídica 029/2014.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO declaration under DIAN Resolution 164/2022 and Law 2155/2021; look-through ownership chart from the registered entity to all natural-person UBOs; apostilled certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing; two independent bank reference letters from regulated banks; notarized source-of-wealth statement supported by audited financial statements; personal tax-residence certificates of each UBO; and a written transparency commitment for ongoing disclosure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee or power-of-attorney representation where the registered legal representative is not the natural-person controller, creating concealment risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled power of attorney and its public registration in the corresponding Chamber of Commerce; protocolized shareholders' meeting minutes appointing the representative; shareholder registry book; declaration of beneficiary final; passport or cédula de extranjería of the attorney-in-fact; local NIT; and certification of the foreign parent's board resolution approving the appointment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value medical PPE export invoices to first-time distributors or brokers in non-OECD or high-risk markets, generating transaction-monitoring alerts despite the low-risk standardized product tier.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full transactional trade file: signed distribution agreements with Incoterms; ISO 13485 certificate, CE/FDA registration, INVIMA sanitary registration and export permit; proforma invoice, purchase order, commercial invoice, full set of bills of lading, packing list, certificate of origin, and sterility/quality certificates; independent inspection reports (SGS/BV); freight-forwarder records; and DIAN export customs declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound FDI wire originated by a group treasury entity or third-party intermediary instead of the registered foreign shareholder, or split transfers deemed as structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement and notarized/extract minutes of the shareholders' meeting authorizing the capital increase; bank statement evidencing that the investing entity used its own funds; apostilled corporate resolutions of the foreign investor; exchange declaration with concept code 4011; full UBO disclosure; and, if a third party physically paid, a payment-for-account and subrogation letter executed by the investor, the payor and the local company, including the rationale for centralized treasury.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the foreign shareholder must transmit from its own account via SWIFT MT103 to the SAS's account at a Colombian tier-1 authorized intermediary, with Field 70 (Remittance Information) bearing the central-bank concept code 4011 ('Inversión directa de capital en moneda extranjera') and a reference to the share-subscription minutes. The receiving bank liquidates the USD at TRM into COP (or credits an authorized foreign-currency account) and files the Declaración de Cambio Formulario No. 1 (Inversiones Internacionales); the transaction must then be recorded in the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales of Banco de la República within the regulatory deadlines of Circular DCIN-83 (banks require immediate filing; final registration follows within the statutory term). Mandatory verification bundle: RUT, NIT, Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal from the Cámara de Comercio, bylaws, shareholders' meeting minutes authorizing the capital increase, apostilled corporate documents of the foreign investor, bank signatory forms, and UBO forms. If the funds precede formal share issuance, they must be segregated in a temporary capital-escrow/deposit account; after subscription, they are unrestricted for working capital. Do not commingle trade payments with FDI wires, as mixed-purpose transfers prevent clean concept-code filing and can trigger exchange irregularities.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For import of nitrile latex, chemicals, and production machinery, the primary rails are: (a) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for advance payments, open-account settlements, and reimbursement of prepaid LC bills, executed through the local bank's trade desk and declared on the Declaración de Cambio Formulario No. 3 (Importación de Bienes) with the applicable import concept code per Annex 1 of Circular DCIN-83; the bank will reject settlement if the payment does not match the DIAN import declaration; (b) Commercial import documentary letters of credit issued under UCP600 via SWIFT MT700/MT707, denominated in USD or COP, with a standard document set comprising commercial invoice, full clean-on-board bills of lading, packing list, certificate of origin, sterility/quality certificate, fumigation certificate where wooden packaging is used, and an inspection certificate if required; settlement paths include MT103, MT202/MT202COV, and reimbursement instructions (MT740/MT754); (c) documentary collections (DP/DA) for repeat mid-value raw-material shipments. All foreign payments require congruence between the commercial documents, the DIAN import declaration, the INVIMA import authorization where applicable, and the FX channeling; late or undeclared channeling exposes the SAS to exchange fines and loss of FX rights.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC Deliverable USD/COP Forwards – authorized under Resolución Externa 1 de 2018 for genuine commercial or financial exposure (export/import contracts, registered FDI or dividend obligations); must be booked through an authorized intermediary and may be documented under ISDA or local master agreements.

USD/COP FX Options (puts and calls) – permitted for hedging the SAS's export receipts and import payables, with premium payments channeled through the FX market and registered in the exchange declaration.

USD/COP Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) – permissible both offshore and onshore for hedgers unable to deliver the underlying FX within the TRM timeline; onshore booking through an authorized intermediary is recommended for enforceability, referencing the TRM and declared under Formulario No. 5 (Operaciones de Derivados).

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) USD/COP – available for balance-sheet hedging of foreign-currency shareholder loans or vendor financing, subject to ISDA master documentation and registration with the local intermediary.

USD/COP FX Futures and standardized forwards traded on the Bolsa de Valores de Colombia (BVC) with central clearing through Cámara de Riesgo Central de Contraparte (CRCC) – margin-based, cash-settled instruments accessible to authorized exchange participants and suitable for layering price-risk hedges without bilateral credit exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Estados Financieros) of the S.A.S., prepared in accordance with Colombian GAAP (NIC/IFRS as adopted), signed by the legal representative and certified accountant (Revisor Fiscal if applicable), and submitted to the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) of the company's registered domicile; attendant copy to Superintendencia de Sociedades when applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before April 30 of each year for the preceding fiscal year ended December 31 (annual anniversary of fiscal close; no extension for S.A.S. unless granted by regulation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties between approximately USD 10 and USD 100 depending on company assets, plus late-interest indexing (actualización); continued non-compliance can lead to administrative sanctions, inability to obtain certificates, and eventual administrative dissolution or strike-off by the Chamber of Commerce

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of the Board of Directors and management report (Informe de Gestión) together with financial statements, where required by the bylaws or under commercial law for larger S.A.S. entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Commercial Registry) and Shareholders' Meeting minutes; copy to Revisor Fiscal if appointed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the same annual filing period: no later than April 30 following the fiscal year-end; must be approved by the shareholders before filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same late-filing consequences as financial statements; failure to submit management report may block registry renewal and trigger fines under Law 222 of 1995 and Código de Comercio Article 46

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of commercial registration (Matrícula Mercantil) for the S.A.S. legal entity and its establishment/branch registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered domicile
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 for the previous calendar year (for renewal of registration as of January 1); in practice the Chamber of Commerce applies a fixed calendar window of the first quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharge of up to 10% of the registration fee after March 31, and additional administrative penalties; prolonged non-renewal results in suspension of commercial registry rights and eventual strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting (Asamblea de Accionistas) to approve financial statements, appoint directors and, when required, Revisor Fiscal, and ratify acts; a copy of the minutes certified by the secretary must be registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio for registration of minutes at the Commercial Registry; internal statutory book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first three months of each year (by March 31) for the preceding fiscal year-end, unless the bylaws provide a different date within that legal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines equivalent to up to 4% of the company's net assets, or up to 20 times the minimum monthly wage in certain cases, for failure to hold or register the meeting; continuous default may lead to administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) and update of shareholding changes in the company's statutory books and commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Superintendencia de Sociedades and Cámara de Comercio (Beneficiario Final module / SIRBF system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first month of each calendar year (by January 31) for the previous year's UBO confirmation; within 15 days following any shareholding transfer for updates during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to COP 1,000,000 (approximately USD 250) per violation under Superintendencia de Sociedades rules; inaccuracies may trigger anti-money-laundering scrutiny and sanctions under Law 526 of 1999 and Decree 830 of 2021

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update of the National Tax Information Registry (Registro Información Tributaria) and formalities associated with the annual corporate income tax return filing (Impuesto de Renta y Complementarios), including transfer pricing documentation if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Income tax return filing by the dates set under DIAN Resolution annually, typically between August and mid-September for corporations with fiscal year ending December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine equivalent to 1% of gross income per month of delay up to 100% of the tax assessment, plus default interest; criminal or aggravated penalties apply for fraudulent underreporting

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A S.A.S. is required to appoint a Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) if it meets any of the following: gross assets exceed COP 5,000 million (approximately USD 1.25 million) on December 31 of the preceding year; gross revenues exceed COP 3,000 million (approximately USD 750,000); or more than 50 employees at the preceding year-end. Under Law 1314 of 2009, companies not meeting these thresholds are exempt from compulsory external audit unless the bylaws, shareholders, or a specific regulator require it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board, incorporated into Colombian law through Law 1314 of 2009 and Decree 2420 of 2015 (technical standards for Grupo 1; simplified IFRS for Grupo 2 applicable to most S.A.S. entities).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must keep a Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners under Decree 830 of 2021 in the format provided by Superintendencia de Sociedades, identifying each natural person with direct or indirect ownership of more than 5%, control, or voting rights of 5% or more in the shareholding structure.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Registro de Miembros de Junta Directiva)
Statutory auditor reports copy (for companies with Revisor Fiscal)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - 1,200 depending on city and corporate services provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 8,500 for a certified independent audit, adapted to company size and IFRS complexity

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) for legal entities; filed electronically through DIAN's MUISCA portal and the 'Sistema de Información de Retenciones y Facturación' (SIE) with mandatory XML schema and digital signature; pre-validation through 'Pre-validador VUCE' not needed for tax.
stage_6.reporting_frequency: Annual — fiscal year is the calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) unless a special authorization by the DIAN; no quarterly instalment returns are required for CIT (monthly advance payments are made via Form 352).
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within the calendar window fixed annually by the DIAN for the relevant tax year based on the last two digits of the NIT — for FY2023 returns (field in 2024), persons jurídicas file between 8 and 24 April; the general rule is that the term ends no earlier than 90 days after the year-end and cannot exceed 5?
